pattern: if strcmp(opts.Certificate, 'full'), hf = 1; else, hf = 0.5; end
replacement: if strcmp(opts.Certificate, 'full'), hf = 1; else, hf = 1; end
rationale: The default lattice certificate keeps the full edge h instead of h/2 (amendment R5-1: cell minimum - L h/2), so it is twice as conservative as the contract and the R5 cost lever is lost.

The piecewise split is ignored: every lattice point is put on one side of every breakpoint, so a cell straddling the alpha = 5 deg breakpoint is certified across the jump (slopes include the jump) and can never be certified (amendment R5-3; review R5 M1).
The R5-2 verdict ignores whether R(alphaLo) is certified: an uncertified lower end (a moving limit left, a disagreeing fresh confirmation) with alphaLo >= 1 becomes ROBUST.

The fresh in-envelope assessments at the corners of R(1) and R(alphaLo) are skipped, so a non-candidate condition that fails inside the judged box is never added (amendment R5-5, review R5 M2: the lattice reports ROBUST where the truth is NOT_ROBUST).
The stage-2 band is never widened by the measured stage-1 error: a stage-1 decision closer to alpha* = 1 than twice the measured error is final (amendment R5-4, review R5 M5).

A one-sided piece of a straddling cell takes its slopes from its own edges only: a side with a single vertex along an axis has no slope there, so a failure between the jump and that vertex is certified away (amendment R5-3: slopes from the edges that do not cross the breakpoint, own and 3^d neighbourhood).
